answer_1.quote: The task of language detoxification is to reduce the risk of generating toxic content in the continuation.
answer_1.outputs: Continuations of prompts with reduced toxicity

answer_2.quote: Following the practice in previous research, we adopt Expected Maximum Toxicity (Exp. Max. Tox.) and Toxicity Probability (Tox. Prob.) to assess the performance of detoxification. ... Besides, we also adopt Perplexity (PPL) to assess the generation fluency.

answer_4.quote: We conduct human evaluation for more comprehensive evaluation. We recruit three graduate students with related background as evaluators. Given the continuations generated by our approach and a compared model for the same prompt, they are asked to choose which one performs better (or select tie) in terms of the following dimensions: (1) Less Toxic: which continuation is less rude, offensive and harmful; (2) More Fluent: which continuation is more well-formed and natural; (3) More Coherent: which continuation has a more consistent language style and topic with the prompt.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators choose which continuation performs better in toxicity, fluency, and coherence.
